Since June fifteenth, twenty twenty-six, neck floats have their own section of the toy rule.
Twelve-fifty point five adds performance tests and warning labels.

caption:
Neck floats for babies got their own section of the US toy rule on June 15, 2026.
16 CFR 1250.5 adds performance and labeling requirements for neck floats, on top of the toy standard in 1250.1 and 1250.2. It covers neck floats for children up to 4 years old, used in sinks, baths and pools.
The float and its packaging carry a set warning, in English, on the principal display panel.
A certificate written before June may cite only the toy standard.

sources.claim: Neck floats: performance + labeling requirements on top of 1250.1/1250.2; up to age 4
sources.quote: This section establishes performance and labeling requirements for neck floats to reduce the risk of children drowning while using a neck float. ... This section adds requirements for neck float in addition to the requirements of §§ 1250.1 and 1250.2. ... Neck float means an article, whether inflatable or not, that encircles the neck, supports the weight of the child by being secured around the neck ... and is intended for use by children up to and including 4 years of age in water environments including sinks, baths, paddling pools, and swimming pools.

sources.claim: Neck float + packaging warnings, English, on the principal display panel
sources.quote: (d) Labeling requirements. All neck floats and the packaging of neck floats must meet the marking, labeling, and instructional literature requirements in this section ... warnings shall be in the English language at a minimum. (iii) The warnings shall be conspicuous and permanent on the principal display panel
